question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on the front tires of a commercial vehicle?
explanation: The manual requires at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires (2/32 inch is the minimum for other tires).
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Tire Problems)

question: According to the manual, how much steering wheel play (about 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel) is enough to make a vehicle hard to steer?
explanation: The manual states steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees, approximately 2 inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel, can make a vehicle hard to steer.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Steering System Defects)

question: A leaf spring will be placed "out of service" if what fraction or more of its leaves are missing?
explanation: The manual notes that if one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle is put "out of service."
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Suspension System Defects)

question: For a vehicle with air brakes, the air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within how many minutes after starting the engine?
explanation: The manual states that air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes of starting the engine.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.1.5 - Seven-step Inspection Method (Step 3, Look at the Gauges)

question: When testing hydraulic brakes for leaks, after pumping the brake pedal three times you should apply firm, steady pressure and hold it for how long?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds to check for a leak.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.1.5 - Seven-step Inspection Method (Step 7, Test for Hydraulic Leaks)

question: Drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo must inspect the cargo's securement within the first how many miles of a trip?
explanation: The manual requires an initial cargo securement check within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or three hours after that, whichever comes first.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.1.6 - Inspection during a Trip (Safety Inspection)

question: Why does the manual recommend backing and turning toward the driver's side whenever possible?
choice_a: It is required by federal regulation
choice_c: It lets the driver watch the rear of the vehicle by looking out the side window
choice_d: It is faster than backing toward the right
explanation: Backing toward the driver's side lets you see better by watching the rear of the vehicle through the side window, since backing to the right is very dangerous because you can't see as well.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.2.4 - Backing Safely

question: The manual lists four basic types of retarders used to help slow a vehicle. Which of these is one of them?
explanation: The manual lists exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric as the four basic types of retarders.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.3.4 - Retarders

question: According to the manual, you should turn off a retarder whenever the road is:
choice_d: In a work zone with a reduced speed limit
explanation: When drive wheels have poor traction, a retarder can cause them to skid, so the retarder should be turned off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.3.4 - Retarders

question: When should you downshift before descending a hill, according to the manual?
choice_a: After your speed has already built up
choice_c: Only when using an automatic transmission
choice_d: Only if there is a posted "steep grade" sign
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to slow down and downshift before starting down a hill, to a gear usually lower than the one needed to climb the same hill.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.3.1 - Manual Transmissions (Basic Procedures for Shifting Down)

question: According to the manual, most good drivers look ahead approximately how many seconds?
explanation: The manual states that most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which is about a quarter mile at highway speeds.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.4.1 - Seeing Ahead

question: What does the manual say about how objects appear in a convex ("fisheye") mirror?
choice_a: They appear larger and closer than they really are
choice_b: They appear at their true size and distance
choice_c: They cannot be seen unless the vehicle is stopped
choice_d: They appear smaller and farther away than they really are
explanation: The manual notes everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would look directly, and things also seem farther away than they really are.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.4.2 - Seeing to the Sides and Rear

question: Which of the following is one of the manual's three rules for using turn signals?
choice_a: Signal continuously and don't cancel it until the turn is complete
choice_b: Signal only after beginning the turn
choice_c: Use your horn instead of a signal when in heavy traffic
choice_d: Cancel your signal before completing the turn
explanation: The manual advises signaling early, signaling continuously through the turn, and not canceling the signal until the turn is complete.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.5.1 - Signal Your Intentions

question: If you must stop on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, in addition to a warning device within 10 feet of the vehicle, how far ahead and behind should you place the other devices?
explanation: On a two-lane, two-way road, warning devices should be placed within 10 feet of the vehicle and 100 feet ahead and behind it.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.5.2 - Communicating Your Presence

question: If you must stop on a one-way or divided highway, warning devices should be placed at 10 feet, 100 feet, and how many feet toward the approaching traffic?
explanation: The manual specifies placing warning devices at 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic on a one-way or divided highway.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.5.2 - Communicating Your Presence

question: At 55 mph, the average driver's perception distance accounts for approximately how many feet traveled?
explanation: The manual states the average perception time is about 1.75 seconds, which accounts for 142 feet traveled at 55 mph.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance

question: At 55 mph, what is the manual's figure for total minimum stopping distance (perception plus reaction plus braking)?
explanation: The manual states that at 55 mph a vehicle will travel a minimum of 419 feet before coming to a complete stop.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance

question: According to the manual, if you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how much greater is the impact of a crash?
explanation: The manual explains that doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph makes the impact and braking distance 4 times greater.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance (Effect of Speed on Stopping Distance)

question: On a wet road, the manual recommends reducing your speed by about how much compared to your dry-road speed (for example, from 55 to about 35 mph)?
explanation: The manual advises reducing speed by about one-third on a wet road, such as slowing from 55 to about 35 mph.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.6.2 - Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: According to the manual, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as:
explanation: The manual states hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water on the road.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.6.2 - Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: The manual's basic following-distance rule for speeds below 40 mph is at least one second for every how many feet of vehicle length?
explanation: The manual's rule of thumb is at least one second of following distance for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.7.1 - Space Ahead

question: If you are driving a 40-foot vehicle at a speed over 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you leave, per the manual's example?
explanation: The manual's example states that over 40 mph, a 40-foot vehicle needs 5 seconds of following distance, versus 4 seconds below 40 mph.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.7.1 - Space Ahead

question: Under move-over laws described in the manual, what should a driver do when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle or roadside incident?
choice_a: Stop completely in the travel lane regardless of traffic
choice_b: Sound the horn continuously while passing
choice_c: Slow down and, if safe, change lanes away from the emergency vehicle or work zone
choice_d: Flash the high beams repeatedly at the emergency vehicle
explanation: The manual explains that move-over laws require drivers to slow and, if safety and traffic conditions permit, change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle or work zone.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.8.2 - Hazardous Roads (Move-Over Laws)

question: According to research cited in the manual, texting while driving makes a CMV driver how many times more likely to be involved in a safety-critical event compared to non-texting drivers?
explanation: The manual cites research showing the odds of a safety-critical event are 23.2 times greater for CMV drivers who text while driving.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.9.5 - Texting

question: A commercial driver's CDL will be disqualified for how long after a second conviction within 3 years for texting while operating a CMV?
explanation: The manual states disqualification is 60 days for a second offense within 3 years and 120 days for three or more offenses within 3 years.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.9.5 - Texting

question: What is the maximum civil penalty the manual describes for a driver who violates the hand-held mobile telephone restriction?
explanation: The manual states violations of the hand-held phone restriction are subject to civil penalties up to $2,750 for drivers, while motor carriers face penalties up to $11,000.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.9.4 - Cell/Mobile Phones

question: According to the manual, what is the first and foremost thing you should do when confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Speed up to stay ahead of them
choice_b: Flash your headlights at them repeatedly
choice_c: Make every attempt to get out of their way
choice_d: Pull over and confront the driver directly
explanation: The manual states that first and foremost, you should make every attempt to get out of an aggressive driver's way.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.10.3 - What You Should Do When Confronted by an Aggressive Driver

question: With low-beam headlights, approximately how far ahead can a driver see at night, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states that with low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet, and with high beams about 350-500 feet.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.11.4 - Vehicle Factors (Headlights)

question: The manual advises dimming your headlights within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to dim their lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.11.5 - Night Driving Procedures

question: According to the manual, getting 6 hours of sleep or less before driving does what to your crash risk?
explanation: The manual states that being sleep-deprived or fatigued, defined as 6 hours of sleep or less, triples your risk of a crash.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.11.2 - Driver Factors (Are You At Risk?)

question: What does the manual say is the best advice regarding driving in fog?
choice_a: Use your high beams for maximum visibility
choice_b: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights to stay on the road
choice_c: Don't drive in fog if you can avoid it
choice_d: Speed up to get through the fog area quickly
explanation: The manual states that the best advice for driving in fog is "don't," and recommends pulling off the road until visibility improves if possible.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.12 - Driving in Fog

question: In very hot weather, the manual recommends inspecting tires how often?
choice_c: Only at the start and end of the trip
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to inspect tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather, since air pressure increases with temperature.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.14.1 - Vehicle Checks (Driving in Very Hot Weather)

question: If there is no stop line painted at a railroad crossing, a vehicle required to stop must stop no closer than how many feet from the nearest rail?
explanation: The manual states vehicles required to stop must stop no closer than 15 feet, and no farther than 50 feet, from the nearest rail.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.15.2 - Warning Signs and Devices (Cross-buck Signs)

question: According to the manual, how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a single railroad track?
explanation: The manual states it takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.15.5 - Crossing the Tracks

question: On a long, steep downgrade, once your speed has been reduced to about 5 mph below your "safe" speed using the brakes, what should you do next?
explanation: The manual's proper braking technique calls for releasing the brakes once speed has been reduced to about 5 mph below the safe speed, then reapplying when it climbs back to the safe speed.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 2.16.4 - Proper Braking Technique
